details: Bootstrap was the exact first shell command requested, including the trailing dot. Its immutable receipt is preserved.
Following shell Python commands installed <=2 CPU affinity, CPU<=120 seconds and AS<=6 GiB before task reads, with external timeout <=140 seconds. Writer has stricter inherited/own limits.

Early read/setup commands before harness had no sampled RSS guard. Later harness sampled self RSS but did not sample every spawned writer/pdftotext child or enforce a sampled-RSS kill threshold. These requirements were not fully met.
PDF processing used subprocess.run with inherited affinity/CPU/AS and bounded per-child timeout; all conversion exit codes were 0 and children reaped. No cgroup/process-group/transient-peak claim.
Resource receipts record self usage, thread join and writer reaping, not comprehensive per-job process-group metrics.

Full raw records were parsed and extracted. All 20 literal statements displayed and read. Initial complete-record output was truncated, so comprehensive human reading of every metadata field is not claimed.

Some broad multi-source excerpt outputs were truncated. The read-*.json ranges from the first broad pass are requested extraction ranges, NOT proof of complete model reading. The smaller targeted displays and ATTEMPTS.md specify actual technical depth.
Search tool responses have service-provided text only; no raw search-response HTTP byte/hash receipt available. HTTP GET receipts are separately saved for all deliberate source fetches.
Journal LLT file GET returned 403; no retry or alternate service query. The route stays unavailable.
No worldwide novelty absence claim. No source/theorem clearance from import roots, titles, registry grep, MathDB open labels or absent solutions. No source completeness from acquisition.
No mathematical enumeration, CAS, solvers, numerics, Lean, formal APIs, delegates, browser, git, installation or out-of-lane writes. Existing protected lanes were not opened/hashed/globbed/polled.
